spec.title: theia PROP-004: Build, watch, lint, test, packaging

status.comment: answers to TYPE-AREA-BUILD; facts 03, 09, 11, 12; implemented in P5, and the install and the scoped compile were run on a real clone of upstream master

facts.THEIA-INSTALL: Dependencies: `npm ci` on Node ≥ 24 with Python 3.13 available for native modules; install runs `node-gyp install`, `theia-patch`, `compute-references` and `lerna run afterInstall` (`03-build-watch-lint-test.md`; `package.json:94-95`). The CI profile's dependency step is `npm ci`; the tree must be byte-identical after it (upstream's own clean-tree gate, `08`).
facts.THEIA-COMPILE: Compile: `lerna run compile` (per package `theiaext compile` = `tsc --project .`) for the whole tree, or `lerna run compile --scope <own package>` for own code; the application bundle is `theia build` in the application directory (esbuild since 1.75.0; webpack is gone - `bundler-generator.ts:43-45`). **Measured in P5**: the contract has no slot for a one-shot compile - the engine compiles through the watch channels and packages through `packageBuild` - so `lerna run compile --scope` is a command of the protocol and of a person, not an answer of the type; both were measured on a real clone in P5: `npm ci` 46 s on the pristine tree, `npm run compile` of the whole tree 68 s over 92 projects, and the own package alone 2 s afterwards. Two facts came out of that measurement and belong to the type's protocol rather than to its answers: **the own package has to be compiled after the tree**, because the compile of a package needs the `lib/` of every package it depends on, and **`npm ci` refuses once the own package exists** (`Missing: <own package> from lock file`), because a workspace member is part of the lockfile - a fork regenerates `package-lock.json` with `npm install` once, carries the result as the tree's own, and `npm ci` is green again from then on.
facts.THEIA-BUILD-CHANNELS: `build up` starts two channels: `typecheck-watch` = `tsc -b -w` at the tree root (project references), `bundle-watch` = `theia build --watch` in the application directory; `build errors` reads their logs; foreign-watcher markers are those two command lines (`03`, watchers).
facts.THEIA-LINT: Lint: `lerna run lint --scope <own package>` (`theiaext lint`, type-aware eslint per package) for the own directory and `npm run lint` for the full tree; the full run is the gate of a phase that adds a package, as `CONF-OWN-EXTENSION-PASSES-THE-FULL-LINT` says for the same reason. **Measured on a real clone in P5 and corrected here**: `lerna run <script> --scope <own package>` cannot reach the own package of a codkit patch set at all - the tool excludes the own root through `.git/info/exclude`, lerna discovers its packages with the git ignores applied, and the run ends in `EFILTER No packages remain after filtering`. The type therefore runs the scripts of the own package by workspace, `npm run lint --workspace <ownRoot>`, which reads the workspace globs of the manifest and finds the package whatever git thinks of it; the full-tree `npm run lint` is upstream's own command and covers every package except that one, which is why the own package is linted first and separately. The same holds for the tests (`THEIA-TEST-RUNNERS`) and for a one-shot compile.
facts.THEIA-TEST-RUNNERS: Three runners (`12-app-test-harness.md`): unit tests `theiaext test` (nyc + mocha over `lib/**/*.spec.js`, selected per package by `lerna run test --scope`); in-page tests `theia test . --test-spec=<glob>` (mocha inside the running frontend with the live container); system tests with `@theia/playwright`. The own-root glob of the CI profile is the package scope, not a path glob. **Implemented in P5**: the contract has one slot for the tests of the own root, and it carries the first runner - `lerna run test --scope <own package>`; the in-page runner and the Playwright suite are a step of the protocol, outside `ci`, exactly as the browser suites of the first type are. The selection is `npm run test --workspace <ownRoot>` for the reason `THEIA-LINT` measured; on a real clone the generated skeleton compiled in 2 s, linted clean in 2 s and its spec passed under nyc with 100% coverage of the two files.
facts.THEIA-PACKAGE-BUILD: Upstream packages no desktop application: no electron-builder configuration, no signing, no installer, no `.icns`/`.ico` generation; its release artefact is npm packages, and its contract with a packager is the built `lib/` of the application (`11-release-packaging.md`). The type's package build is therefore `theia build` of the application; the installer is a product artifact (the product declares its packager and its config in its own delta), and the type's `ci --profile build` ends at the built application unless the product declares more.
facts.THEIA-NO-STAMPS: Nothing is stamped at build time - no sha, no date, no quality channel (`09-build-time-stamps.md`); what is baked into `src-gen/` is the frontend and backend configuration, the page title and the extension inventory. A product that wants a commit in its About dialog adds it through its own package (a generated constant written by `load` from the pin), not through the type.
facts.THEIA-OWN-ROOT-CARRIES-ITS-BUILD-OUTPUT: **Measured on a real clone in P5 as a defect of the engine; answered in P5-2.** The own root of this family is a *compiled npm package*, so its build output lands **inside** it - `packages/<own>/lib/`, `.eslintcache`, `*.tsbuildinfo`. The engine treats every file under the own root as own code, and the fresh pass deliberately never cleans inside it (own code is not litter), so after one compile `status` reports the compiled `lib/` as own code the tree has and the delta does not, and `load` refuses over it as a dirty tree. The contract now lets a type say which paths inside an owned directory a build writes (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-LAYOUT`), and this type says it: inside the own package `lib/**`, `node_modules/**`, `.nyc_output/**`, `coverage/**`, `.eslintcache`, `*.tsbuildinfo`; inside the application the same plus `src-gen/**`, `plugins/**` and the generated bundler entries. The coverage state was measured on the real clone in P5-2: the test runner of this family writes `.nyc_output/` inside the owned directory, exactly as the compiler writes `lib/`. The engine never copies them into the delta, never counts them as changed own code, never removes them on a load, and removes them on `load --fresh`; the hand protocol of P5 (delete them before every command) is retired. The first type never met this because its own code compiles into `out/` outside the own root.
